items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: Angel City Drum Works is the name of the company and they have like – I think I’m the only percussion player they have, but they have a lot of drummers. Erskine, Peter Erskine, JR, a bunch of cats.

ctx.x: Do you have a cartage system? You know have people move stuff around for you?

Yeah. Angel City Drum Works is the name of the company and they have like – I think I’m the only percussion player they have, but they have a lot of drummers. Erskine, Peter Erskine, JR, a bunch of cats. And they take us around in the studios. But the new world now is having a home recording studio you know. So I have one and thank God I’ve been pretty busy about it, with it. And a lot of sessions happen now that you don’t go anywhere, you just do them here. Overdubs.

Yeah. They send you a track and you can add. Yeah. I have another quote here. I’m sure the studio scene, as you mentioned, has changed a lot. And this is from your James Taylor bandmate, Lou Marini. And he was talking about the way songs are put together these days, and he said, “When I listen to these vocoder vocals and the rhythm tracks you could just as easily be listening to a washing machine. Luis Conte is a master percussionist. He’s always playing stuff for us from African tribal music, Caribbean,…
